questions.q: What language is a Step Functions state machine defined in?
options: Amazon States Language (ASL), a JSON-based format
YAML CloudFormation templates
Python
A drag-and-drop-only format with no underlying text representation
questions.explain: State machines are defined in ASL, a JSON-based language describing states and the transitions between them.

questions.q: In ASL, how does a state indicate it is the last one in the machine?
options: It sets "End": true instead of a "Next" field
It omits the "Type" field
It must be named "Final"
State machines cannot end — they run forever
questions.explain: Every state either transitions with "Next" to another state, or terminates the machine with "End": true.

questions.q: You're orchestrating a nightly pipeline (Glue crawler, then Glue ETL job, then a Lambda notification) that takes about 20 minutes and needs a durable, inspectable history the next morning. Which workflow type fits?
options: Standard — long-running, exactly-once, full execution history
Express — built for sub-5-minute, high-volume event processing
Neither type supports Glue as a Task state
Standard workflows cannot exceed 5 minutes either
questions.explain: Standard workflows support runs up to a year, exactly-once semantics, and a full auditable execution history — exactly what a 20-minute nightly pipeline with post-mortem needs calls for.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of Step Functions over just having one Lambda function invoke another to chain steps?
options: Orchestration logic — retries, timeouts, branching, error handling — becomes visible and declarative instead of buried in application code
Step Functions is the only way to invoke a Lambda function at all
Lambda functions cannot call AWS APIs directly
It removes the need for IAM roles entirely
questions.explain: The core value is that the orchestration itself — not just the steps — becomes visible in a state machine definition and in the console's execution diagram, rather than being scattered across function code.

questions.q: Which of these is true of Express workflows but NOT Standard workflows?
options: Maximum execution duration of 5 minutes and at-least-once semantics
Can run for up to one year
Keeps a full, detailed execution history for every run
Priced strictly per state transition
questions.explain: Express workflows cap out at 5 minutes, use at-least-once semantics, and are priced by execution count/duration rather than per transition — a tradeoff aimed at high-volume, short-lived event processing.
